promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Cell structure: comparing plant and animal cells
Cell structure: functions of cell structures

questions.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: A cellulose cell wall is present in plant cells but absent from animal cells, which have only a cell membrane.

questions.q: The cell wall of a plant cell is made mainly of which substance?
questions.explain: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, which strengthens and supports the cell.

questions.q: Which of these structures is present in BOTH plant and animal cells?
questions.explain: Mitochondria occur in both plant and animal cells; chloroplasts, permanent vacuoles and cell walls are found only in plant cells.

questions.q: Why do palisade cells in a leaf contain many chloroplasts but human red blood cells contain none?
options: Only plant cells carry out photosynthesis
Red blood cells have cell walls instead
questions.explain: Chloroplasts are needed for photosynthesis, which occurs in plant cells but not in animal cells.

questions.q: A cell is examined and found to have a nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria and a cell membrane, but no cell wall or chloroplasts. It is most likely which type of cell?
questions.explain: The absence of a cell wall and chloroplasts, together with a true nucleus, indicates an animal cell.

questions.q: What is the function of the nucleus in a cell?
options: Controls cell activities and contains genetic material
Controls entry and exit of substances
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the genetic material (DNA) and controls the cell's activities.

questions.q: Which structure is the site of aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy for the cell.

questions.q: What is the main function of ribosomes?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.q: The cell membrane controls which substances enter and leave the cell. This property is best described as being:
questions.explain: The cell membrane is partially permeable, allowing some substances through while blocking others.

questions.q: Which structure keeps a plant cell firm by being filled with cell sap?
questions.explain: The large permanent vacuole is filled with cell sap and helps keep the plant cell firm (turgid).

questions.q: Chloroplasts are able to absorb light energy because they contain:
questions.explain: Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which structure is found in a bacterial cell but not in a plant or animal cell?
questions.explain: Bacterial cells contain plasmids (small rings of DNA), which are not found in plant or animal cells.

questions.q: How is the genetic material arranged in a bacterial cell?
options: As a circular loop of DNA
questions.explain: Bacterial cells contain a single circular loop of DNA that is not enclosed in a nucleus.

questions.q: Which set of structures is found in a typical bacterial cell?
options: Cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, circular DNA, plasmids
questions.explain: A bacterial cell has a cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, circular DNA and plasmids, but no nucleus, mitochondria or chloroplasts.

questions.q: Why is a bacterial cell unable to carry out aerobic respiration in the same way as an animal cell using mitochondria?
options: Bacterial cells do not contain mitochondria
questions.explain: Bacterial cells lack mitochondria, so they do not carry out respiration using these organelles.

questions.q: The formula for magnification is:
questions.explain: Magnification is calculated by dividing the image size by the actual size of the specimen.

questions.q: A drawing of a cell measures 40 mm across. The actual cell is 0.5 mm across. What is the magnification?
questions.explain: Magnification = image size / actual size = 40 / 0.5 = 80.

questions.q: A cell is drawn at a magnification of ×100. The image measures 6 mm. What is the actual size of the cell?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size / magnification = 6 / 100 = 0.06 mm.

questions.q: A cell has an actual length of 0.05 mm. Converted into micrometres (µm), this length is:
A student measures the image of a specimen as 8 mm and calculates its actual size as 4 mm. What magnification did the microscope drawing use?
questions.explain: Magnification = image size / actual size = 8 / 4 = 2.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus; Organisation of the Organism
